sn.s: Un viernes me roban el celular.
sn.e: One Friday my phone gets stolen.

sn.s: Pasa en el bus, apretado entre la gente.
sn.e: It happens on the bus, squeezed among the people.

sn.s: No siento nada.
sn.e: I feel nothing.

sn.s: Me bajo y el bolsillo está vacío.
sn.e: I get off and my pocket is empty.

sn.s: Lo primero que pienso es en español.
sn.e: The first thing I think is in Spanish.

sn.s: Y lo pienso mal.
sn.e: And I think it wrong.

sn.s: "Yo perdí mi celular", digo yo.
sn.e: "I lost my phone," I say.

sn.s: Marcos me corrige enseguida.
sn.e: Marcos corrects me straight away.

sn.s: "No lo perdiste. Te lo robaron."
sn.e: "You didn't lose it. It was stolen from you."

sn.s: Y ahí hay una lección entera.
sn.e: And there is a whole lesson in that.

sn.s: En español las cosas malas le pasan a uno.
sn.e: In Spanish bad things happen to you.

sn.s: Uno no las hace.
sn.e: You do not do them.

sn.s: Se me perdió la llave.
sn.e: The key got lost on me.

sn.s: Se me cayó el vaso.
sn.e: The glass fell on me.

sn.s: Se me olvidó el mandado.
sn.e: The errand got forgotten on me.

sn.s: Se me quedó la bolsa en la casa.
sn.e: The bag stayed behind on me at the house.

sn.s: En todas la culpa está en otro lado.
sn.e: In all of them the blame is somewhere else.

sn.s: En mi idioma yo digo yo lo perdí.
sn.e: In my language I say I lost it.

sn.s: Aquí se dice que se perdió solo.
sn.e: Here you say it lost itself.

sn.s: Al principio eso me parecía una excusa.
sn.e: At first that seemed like an excuse to me.

sn.s: Ahora me parece otra cosa.
sn.e: Now it seems like something else.

sn.s: Aquí pasan muchas cosas que uno no controla.
sn.e: Here a lot of things happen that you do not control.

sn.s: Se va la luz. Se va el agua.
sn.e: The power goes. The water goes.

sn.s: Se descompone el bus.
sn.e: The bus breaks down.

sn.s: Se cae el techo con la lluvia.
sn.e: The roof goes with the rain.

sn.s: Y un idioma que vive así habla así.
sn.e: And a language that lives like that talks like that.

sn.s: Doña Carmen me pregunta si voy a denunciar.
sn.e: Doña Carmen asks if I am going to report it.

sn.s: "¿Sirve de algo?", pregunto yo.
sn.e: "Is it any use?" I ask.

sn.s: Ella hace una cara.
sn.e: She pulls a face.

sn.s: "Sirve para el papel", dice ella.
sn.e: "It's useful for the paperwork," she says.

sn.s: "Para el celular, no."
sn.e: "For the phone, no."

sn.s: No voy a denunciar.
sn.e: I do not report it.

sn.s: Nadie de la calle denuncia esas cosas.
sn.e: Nobody on the street reports things like that.

sn.s: Roberto me dice lo que se hace.
sn.e: Roberto tells me what you do.

sn.s: "Se compra otro usado y ya."
sn.e: "You buy another second-hand one and that's that."

sn.s: Al otro día don Beto llega a mi casa.
sn.e: The next day don Beto arrives at my house.

sn.s: Trae un celular viejo en la mano.
sn.e: He brings an old phone in his hand.

sn.s: "Era de mi hijo", dice él.
sn.e: "It was my son's," he says.

sn.s: "Está feo pero sirve."
sn.e: "It's ugly but it works."

sn.s: Yo trato de pagarle.
sn.e: I try to pay him.

sn.s: Don Beto no lo acepta.
sn.e: Don Beto will not accept it.

sn.s: "Después me hace otro favor", dice él.
sn.e: "You'll do me another favour some time," he says.

sn.s: Ese celular me dura dos años.
sn.e: That phone lasts me two years.

sn.s: Después Marcos me enseña la otra regla.
sn.e: Later Marcos teaches me the other rule.

sn.s: "El celular en la mano es un regalo."
sn.e: "A phone in your hand is a gift."

sn.s: "En el bolsillo de adelante, no."
sn.e: "In your front pocket, it isn't."

sn.s: Yo lo llevo en el bolsillo de adelante desde entonces.
sn.e: I have carried it in my front pocket ever since.

sn.s: Con la mano encima, sin pensarlo.
sn.e: With my hand over it, without thinking.
